transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Ruiz (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood CSM), Talia Nguyen (Redwood Product), Priya Shah (Nautilus Head of ML), Ethan Morgan (Platform Eng), Juno Park (FinOps), Leo Daniels (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
QBR style check-in focused on usage trends, cost 'burn' forecasting cadence, recent latency/regression event in staging, and roadmap alignment. Action items assigned for burst testing on dedicated pool, sharing 90-day traffic profile, and providing SOC2/KMS info. Discussed tradeoffs between Dedicated vs Hosted for peak/internal inference, and potential private deployment for regulated PHI flows.

Topics noted: usage patterns, burst behavior, cost optimization, KV cache effectiveness, dedicated capacity sizing, SOC2/SSO/KMS questions, pilot SLA dashboard access, next procurement steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, we've got about 50 minutes, big agenda is a quick QBR style checkin on ops and then dig into the burn forecasting cadence you asked for, so, Priya, want to kick us off with a quick update on where Nautilus is running today?
[00:18] Priya: yeah, thanks Samir, uh so we're at about 2.1M tokens/day on average, charts are in the sheet, weekends dip to like 1.1M, and we see a recurring spike every Wednesday around midday, that's where the peaker shows. also, internal inference for triage is on our own infra but customer-facing flows are on Redwood hosted for now.
[00:36] Ethan: quick clarif - the hosted calls are the ones with PII stripped, but for PHI we route to our private VPC demo cluster right? there's still some confusion across the infra team about which endpoints are in VPC.
[00:50] Samir: correct, today you have a hybrid setup — hosted for non-sensitive, private (Redwood Private) for PHI. We also recommended a dedicated pool for the high-volume routing to minimize cost and tail latency.
[01:05] Juno: from FinOps side we're trying to forecast burn. last quarter surprised us with a 28% delta when Wednesday spikes combined with longer context lengths. we need a predictable cadence and a template for capacity planning.
[01:20] Marcus: totally, that's what the burn forecasting template is for, Samir and I can send you a monthly cadence that maps token trend + burst headroom to a recommended reserved capacity band.
[01:33] Priya: awesome. also, we saw the staging regression last week — saw a 40ms p50 increase for the 8k context chat variant. Elena, I think you were investigating?
[01:47] Elena: yeah, I dug in — initial hypothesis was KV chache thrash during concurrent prefix loads, there was an unexpected eviction pattern when multiple large contexts hit the same shard. we tuned the cache window and bumped the KV store memory reservation on the Dedicated pool and saw latency drop back down. logs attached in the ticket, though some stack traces had garbled model names in the logging.
[02:10] Leo: security wants to get clarity on KMS and key custody — if we move more PHI to Redwood Private we need HSM/KMS integration specifics and audit log retention periods.
[02:23] Samir: documented — we'll include the KMS integration note in the pack. Redwood supports customer-managed keys via cloud KMS and we can provide the HSM summary; Marcus will share the SOC two attestation snapshot.
[02:36] Talia: quick product note — we've been rolling out smarter batching heuristics in the runtime; for bursty workloads you might see better unit cost with auto-batching enabled plus prefix caching. but if you need strict p95 SLOs the dedicated pool and pinning model versions gives more predictable latency.
[02:58] Priya: can you remind me the expected cost delta for auto-batching vs dedicated pinning? numbers would help Juno.
[03:06] Samir: rough rule of thumb — auto-batching can shave 20-35% off per-token cost depending on request shape, but it can add 10-50ms to p95 in some cases. Dedicated reserved capacity reduces variability and can be cheaper when you're above sustained throughput thresholds. We'll run a tailored forecast for your Wednesday spike.
[03:30] [sound of typing/background noise]
[03:40] Juno: hypothetically, if we committed to a Q4 reserved band, what's the lead time to spin up extra GPUs for the dedicated pool? we need to align procurement.
[03:51] Elena: depends on config — standard Gpu types we can add capacity within 2-3 weeks for Dedicated; private on-prem deliveries are longer. There's also a burst queue option for short windows.
[04:05] Priya: about the KV cache issue — is that specific to certain model families? our stack uses a mix of open-weights models and some redwood-verified ones.
[04:16] Elena: it's more request-shape specific than model family, but quantized weights + long context windows exacerbate memory pressure. we recommended revising prefix caching TTLs for those routes.
[04:30] Ethan: can we get a sampling of the logs that show the eviction? for our infra team to model it.
[04:36] Elena: yes I'll upload a sanitized log dump, might be a little noisy — note that transcriptions in some logs show 'Redwood Dedicate' spelled weird in the agent messages.
[04:50] Samir: ok let's shift to the burn cadence — Juno, what's your preferred cadence for a burn forecast? monthly? biweek?
[04:58] Juno: monthly is ok, but we want a weekly quick-check summary for spikes during release periods. so monthly deep forecast + weekly pulse.
[05:09] Marcus: we'll produce a monthly forecast template and a lightweight weekly pulse email that includes actual vs forecast and recommended action (reduce batch window, bump reserved band, or enable burst capacity).
[05:21] Priya: in the weekly pulse can you include a model drift quality signal? we want to tie cost-to-quality so we don't over-optimize for cost.
[05:31] Talia: yep, we can tie quality regressions to prompt sets — Redwood Optimize can flag regression on a small eval suite and include it in the pulse.
[05:40] Leo: security note — audit logs retention and export cadence must meet our compliance window of 2 years, is that supported?
[05:49] Samir: yes, we can extend retention for enterprise accounts; we'll include export options and a sample retention schedule in the security pack.
[05:59] [06:00] Priya: timeline question: procurement wants to know final pricing by next Friday so they can include it in the Q4 commit — can we do that?
[06:10] Samir: yes we'll get a committed band estimate by 2027-08-27. I'll include a couple of reserved tiers and the delta vs pay-as-you-go.
[06:19] Juno: and please surface the breakout: base tokens, embeddings, and any outbound egress/network costs.
[06:28] Samir: totally.
[06:31] Elena: technical note: for the burst test we'll provision a temporary dedicated pool with the same instance shapes and run a 6-hour synthetic load — we'll publish p50/p95/p99 and KV metrics.
[06:44] Ethan: that helps, can you include the exact API endpoints we'll hit so ops can allowlist them?
[06:50] Elena: yes, will include list and a short curl script.
[06:55] [07:02] Marcus: re: SLA dashboard access — I'll create a read-only role for Nautilus in the pilot console, so your SREs can see token-level breakdowns and per-route latency.
[07:13] Priya: appreciate that. on roadmap alignment, we want to know if Redwood plans any infra churn or model deprecations in the next 90 days that could affect rollouts.
[07:25] Talia: short answer: planned model catalog updates in mid-September include deprecating one 4-bit quantized runtime for an optimized 4-bit path — we'll send a compatibility notice and migration guidance. No infra-wide node replacement is planned during your Q4 window.
[07:41] Priya: thanks.
[07:45] [08:00] Juno: can we see a sample monthly forecast? maybe an example that shows how we map Wednesday spikes into reserved bands and cost delta.
[08:09] Samir: yes Elena and I will prepare a Nautilus-tailored sheet — example bands: Band A (baseline) 0-1.5M tokens/day, Band B (committed) 1.5-3M, Band C (high) 3M+, with recommended reserved GPU targets and estimated monthly spend.
[08:28] Priya: if we pick Band B, what's the rollover policy if we underutilize? we don't want to overcommit.
[08:35] Samir: we have quarterly true-ups — optionally you can set a flexible band with a smaller discount but no hard annual lock. We'll detail options.
[08:46] Leo: security follow-up: SAML SSO integration — need an SP metadata example and identity mapping doc for our Okta setup.
[08:54] Marcus: I'll attach the SAML recipe and example attribute mapping.
[09:00] [09:20] Priya: any concerns about vendor lock if we move more to Redwood Private? some of our architects worry about portability.
[09:29] Talia: reasonable question — deployment abstraction is meant to keep APIs consistent and we provide a model artifacts export and inference config templates so you can replicate behavior elsewhere if needed. We'll point to the model export guide.
[09:45] Elena: also, the KV cache behavior is documented with tuning knobs so you can reproduce performance in a different runtime if you choose.
[09:52] [10:10] Juno: procedural ask — for procurement we'll need a one-pager that lists SLA targets, billing cadence, cancellation windows, and contact for support escalation.
[10:20] Samir: yes we'll produce a concise 'commercial one-pager' and attach it to the price sheet.
[10:28] [10:35] Priya: small question — do you have a recommended config for the Wednesday spike that reduces overall cost but keeps p95 under 600ms?
[10:44] Elena: two-pronged — enable prefix caching for those routes, set a moderate batching window (25-40ms), and a dedicated small reserved band to absorb consistent load; that combo usually keeps p95 in the 400-600ms range.
[10:58] Ethan: will that impact throughput for other tenants on Hosted?
[11:03] Talia: if you move that traffic to Dedicated, no, Hosted tenant interference is avoided. If you keep on Hosted with batching, you might see fluctuating p95 across tenants.
[11:17] [11:30] Marcus: ok wrapping toward next steps — quick recap of who owns what.
[11:36] Samir: recap: Elena — run burst test and upload logs (Due 2027-09-01). Priya — share 90-day traffic CSV (Due 2027-08-30). Samir — send pricing sheet, burn template, SOC2 snapshot and KMS note (Due 2027-08-27). Juno — confirm Q4 budget band (Due 2027-09-07). Marcus — set up pilot dashboard and attach SAML recipe (Due 2027-08-29).
[11:58] Priya: all good, is there a preferred format for the 90-day CSV?
[12:05] Marcus: column set — timestamp, route, model, token_count, user_id (hashed), error_flag. we'll paste a small template in the notes.
[12:17] Samir: final note: competitors were mentioned — you said you were also validating Anthropic and Vertex for price/perf; feel free to share findings and we'll highlight where Redwood's guaranteed SLOs and observability map to your needs.
[12:33] Juno: yeah we're doing that in parallel. doesn't change immediate timeline.
[12:40] Samir: great, thanks all. We'll follow up with the attachments and scheduled calendar for the burst test.
[12:48] Leo: thanks everyone.
[12:50] [End of recording]
